title: Stable route onboarding scraps and copy experiments
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick, messy working notes capturing UX ideas, wireframe fragments, and copy variants for the model -> endpoint -> stable-version onboarding path. Focus: reduce friction when teams create an endpoint and pick a model + stable version that guarantees predictable behavior (rollback, canary, fallback). This is intentionally granular — use to seed a PRD and a small A/B test later.

CONTEXT & ASSUMPTIONS:
- Customers want a straightforward way to surface a single model version as the canonical production variant (we call it 'stable' here) while keeping the ability to stage new versions.
- Current console flows surface models and versions but bury the act of making one version the default for an endpoint.
- Goal: 3-click happy path from: Create endpoint -> pick model family -> choose stable version -> confirm.
- Must be compatible with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (visibility differences noted below).

HIGH-LEVEL JOURNEY (user intent):
1) Create endpoint (name, description, route)
2) Select model family (search, filters: size, latency tier, quantization available)
3) Pick a version (list with performance badges and pinned/stable affordance)
4) Confirm stable version with release options (immediate, canary %, scheduled)
5) Endpoint created with explicit stable version pinned; UI shows rollback and promote actions.

WIREFRAME SCRAPS (annotated notes, not visual files):
- Top-level stepper: [Endpoint details] -> [Model] -> [Version & Release] -> [Review]
  - Rationale: linear mental model; prevents accidental omission of stable selection.
- Model card: compact card with micro-metrics row: (avg latency / tokens, throughput, cost-est / 1k tokens). Click card expands to version table.
- Version table (row per version): columns: version id, performance badge, last-eval-summary (short), deployed-locations, size/quant, three-action menu (Set stable, Compare, View changelog).
- 'Set stable' CTA inline (ghost button). Hover tooltip: "Mark this version as the endpoint's stable behavior. Traffic will route here unless a canary is configured."
- When user clicks Set stable -> open a micro-modal with release knobs: Immediate (all traffic), Canary (slider 0-50%), Schedule (datetime). Defaults: Immediate. Micro-modal copy: see COPY OPTIONS section.

MICROCOPY VARIANTS (split-test candidates):
- Confirmation header options:
  1) "Promote version v1.3 to stable for this endpoint"
  2) "Use v1.3 as the endpoint’s stable model"
  3) "Make v1.3 the default for production traffic"
- Help line under header: "Stable = pinned, predictable outputs; rollouts and canary options available."
- Buttons: Primary: [Promote now] / Secondary: [Cancel]. Alternative primary label: [Set as stable].
- Canary slider helper: "Start with X% traffic to verify quality — rollback available instantly."
- Post-create toast: "Endpoint created — v1.3 is stable. You can promote, rollback, or open a canary from the endpoint page."

COMPARISON MODE (quick UX idea):
- Small diff panel that compares two versions: prompt-level examples (same canned prompt), token-level delta (avg length), sample outputs with highlighted divergences. Link to run a quick eval with your prompt set.

EDGE CASES & DECISIONS:
- What happens when a stable version is deleted? Two options: prevent deletion (soft-block) OR auto-unset stable and warn. Recommendation: prevent deletion of a stable version unless user explicitly reassigns stable or confirms deletion with a second confirmation.
- Multiple endpoints pointing at same model version: treat stable flag per endpoint, not global.
- Private deployments: stable toggle may require additional approval or an audit log entry visible in the endpoint timeline. Add a small badge: [private: audit required] and call out KMS/HSM differences in the review step.
- Confusing copy: avoid 'pin' verb in customer-facing text — 'set as stable' or 'promote' preferred. Internal docs can keep 'pin' language.

BACKLOG GROOM NOTES (tickets to create / refine):
- UX-XXXX: Add 'Set as stable' inline affordance in version table (acceptance: visible to users who have endpoint edit permissions).
- UX-XXXX: Micro-modal release knobs with canary slider + schedule option.
- ENG-XXXX: Prevent deletion of stable versions; surface explicit block in API/console.
- PLATFORM-XXXX: Add audit event for stable assignment (private deployments require explicit audit record).
- SRE-XXXX: Metric to emit: stable_version_change events with user, endpoint id, old/new version, canary_pct.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (MVP):
- User can create an endpoint and set a version as stable during creation in the 3rd step.
- Stable selection persists and is shown on endpoint summary (version id + badge).
- Users with edit rights can change stable version via the endpoint settings and are prompted for canary/confirm.
- Deleting a stable version is blocked with a clear message.
- Audit event emitted for every stable change.

OPEN QUESTIONS (requires product/engineering sync):
- Default release pattern: should we default to Immediate or Canary 5%? Ops worry about immediate rollouts causing regressions in heavy-use endpoints. Suggest default Canary 10% for endpoints with >1000 req/day.
- Should stable assignment be allowed via API only or must be surfaced in console? Both; but console UX must show permission hints.
- How to surface cost delta between versions for non-engine users? Add a small cost tooltip but keep it low-friction.

COPY EXAMPLES (full-length for review):
- On endpoint summary when stable present: "Stable model: v1.3 — Promoted by Asha on 2025-02-03 • View changelog • Promote new"
- On history timeline entry: "Asha set v1.3 as stable (immediate) — audit id: P-20250203-03"
- Modal help text: "Stable version pins a specific model artifact to this endpoint so production traffic receives consistent behavior. You can run a canary, schedule a promotion, or roll back at any time."

QUICK UX EXPERIMENTS (low-effort A/B):
- A: Inline 'Set as stable' button on each version row (visible, concise).
- B: Require explicit 'Promote' micro-modal from a right-side details rail (more deliberate, fewer accidental clicks).
- Measure: time-to-first-stable after endpoint creation, number of rollbacks in first 24h, mistaken promotions (defined as immediate rollback < 10m).

NEXT STEPS FOR SPRINT PLANNING:
- Clean up copy variants and pick top 2 for UI team to build into Figma (owner: Priya).
- Create the tickets listed above and assign owners (deadline: sprint planning).
- Quick sync with SRE/Platform on metric names and audit schema (owner: Ben).
- Prototype micro-modal in console sandbox and run internal dogfood with solutions-eng team.

NOTES-TO-SELF:
- Keep 'stable' human-friendly; avoid jargon.
- Add keyboard shortcut for promoting if power users ask for it later.

END.
